title: State v. N.S. Container Logistics (Nhava Sheva Warehouse Arson / Fire Inquest)
citation: Independent Contributor: Forensic Law Student Moot Archive (Case #BLIND-2024-F01)
confidence_note: Moderate - Mixed circumstantial financial motive vs physical fire science

ground_truth.rationale: Forensic fire burn-pattern analysis and contractor job sheets confirm uninsulated hot-slag from structural welding ignited open lacquer thinner barrels. Owner's vehicle departed 2 hours prior.

hypotheses.label: Managing Director Rajesh G. (Arson Insurance Fraud)
hypotheses.statement: Director arranged deliberate torching of warehouse to recover ₹45 Crore fire insurance policy to clear impending commercial bank defaults.

hypotheses.label: Contractor Maintenance Welding Crew (Gross Negligence)
hypotheses.statement: Uncertified welding workers operated thermal cutting torch adjacent to volatile chemical storage without mandatory fire-retardant blankets or standby extinguishers.

hypotheses.label: Electrical Substation Surge / Transformer Failure
hypotheses.statement: High-voltage monsoon power fluctuation in the main terminal transformer triggered electrical arcing in ceiling conduits causing passive structural ignition.

H2.mo_description: Failed to erect fire-resistant partition walls during hot-cutting operations near solvent drums.

exhibits.name: State Fire Services Forensic Arson & Burn Origin Investigation
exhibits.text: Detailed inverted V-pattern thermal mapping isolates the primary fire origin to Bay-4 welding partition at floor level. Gas chromatography confirmed absence of kerosene or commercial accelerants; fuel source was unsealed industrial lacquer thinner barrels ignited by 1200°C molten welding slag. Electrical conduit breakers on the main transformer were tripped mechanically post-fire, disproving electrical failure as the initiator.

exhibits.name: Contractor Hot-Work Job Card & Disciplinary Inspection
exhibits.text: Maintenance job ticket confirms Apex Contractors crew was performing uninsulated torch-cutting of steel shelving in Bay-4 until 19:55. Safety auditor inspection reveals two handheld chemical extinguishers beside Bay-4 were discharged and completely empty prior to the incident, with zero water hoses connected.

exhibits.name: Perimeter Gate ANPR & Director Vehicle Log
exhibits.text: High-definition ANPR camera captures Director Rajesh G.'s Mercedes departing the facility at 18:22 IST. Cellular tower records corroborate his device registered at a business club dinner in South Mumbai from 19:30 onwards through midnight, establishing physical absence during the 20:15 ignition window.

exhibits.name: Commercial Insurance Policy & Bank Debt Recovery Notice
exhibits.text: Financial audit records demonstrate warehouse inventory was insured for ₹45 Crore with policy renewed 3 weeks prior. State Bank had served an asset possession notice under SARFAESI Act for ₹38 Crore pending debt, creating strong circumstantial suspicion of financial motive.

adversarial_exhibit.name: Anonymous Tipster Note Accusing Director
adversarial_exhibit.text: Unsigned computer-printed note dropped at police station claiming Director Rajesh met professional torchmen at a hotel.
